column3: Permission checks are scoped honestly: for shipped and built-in rows they hold against accidental reach on every service lookup path (internal/get hook, a reflect.get wrapper, a re-attributed ctx.root, caller checks in secrets/ops/wire, module-private service state), with Cordis escape hatches and computed imports refused at build for local and npm packages; a market code install runs with owner trust and its permissions describe what it declares, not a sandbox
column4: plugins share one isolate, so in-isolate checks cannot make untrusted code safe (Bosun, 2026-11-16); private fields cannot hide state behind Cordis's method proxies
